theme: 3 terms on array methods that take a closure: change every item, keep some items and combine all items into one value

terms.definition: A collection method that changes every item and returns the results in a new array.
terms.example: Use map to turn the user list into an array of names.

terms.definition: A collection method that keeps only the items passing a test and returns them in a new array.
terms.example: Use filter to keep only the unread messages.

terms.definition: A collection method that combines all the items into one value, starting from a first value.
terms.example: Use reduce to add up every price in the cart.

video.title: Map, Filter & Reduce in 2 minutes | iOS Daily English Day 25
video.description:
Learn to talk about Swift array methods that replace long loops: Map, Filter & Reduce, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Map - A collection method that changes every item and returns the results in a new array.
Filter - A collection method that keeps only the items passing a test and returns them in a new array.
Reduce - A collection method that combines all the items into one value, starting from a first value.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Day 25 of the iOS Daily English series: 3 terms a day, from Swift basics to advanced iOS.

Explain Map, Filter & Reduce in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
맵, 필터, 리듀스 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Map - A collection method that changes every item and returns the results in a new array.
한국어: 맵: 모든 항목을 바꿔서 결과를 새 배열로 돌려주는 컬렉션 메서드

Filter - A collection method that keeps only the items passing a test and returns them in a new array.
한국어: 필터: 조건을 통과한 항목만 남겨 새 배열로 돌려주는 컬렉션 메서드

Reduce - A collection method that combines all the items into one value, starting from a first value.
한국어: 리듀스: 시작 값에서 출발해 모든 항목을 하나의 값으로 합치는 컬렉션 메서드

dialogue.title: One long loop, three short lines

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mina, my loop over `prices` is so long. It picks the big ones, halves them, then adds them up.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three steps, three methods. First, use Filter to keep the prices that are ten or more.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I tried Map for that, but I got an array of `true` and `false`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the mistake. Map changes every item. Filter keeps or drops items.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, so Filter gives me `big`, with only three prices.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. Now use Map on `big` to cut each price in half.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, you get a new array, `sale`. Last, use Reduce to add everything into `total`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Why does Reduce start with zero?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the first value. Each price is added to it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Got it. Filter to pick, Map to change, Reduce to combine.
